title: Roadmaps, pricing your product work, and measuring launches

say: Roadmaps, pricing your product work, and measuring launches.
This is the video for module three of Product Management Foundations.
Product work succeeds or fails in conversations with stakeholders. A roadmap built without understanding the business, the people and the politics will be ignored or overturned.

panel.heading: Product work lives in conversations
items: Understand the people and the politics

say: In this module you learn to build an honest roadmap, price and scope paid product work, and measure results after launch. You finish with a case study outline and a 90-day plan.

panel.heading: Product work lives in conversations
items: Understand the people and the politics

say: For example, Ifeoma joins a school-payments start-up in Port Harcourt as its first PM. The founder hands her 18 requested features with promised dates.

After six stakeholder conversations, she groups the features under problems. Now holds the problem that is understood: parents forget due dates. Next holds what is being explored. Later holds instalments, which need a licensed partner.
Each item is a problem, not a feature, and only Now gets target months. That is honest about uncertainty.
When evidence changes a priority, tell the affected stakeholders first, in person or by a short call. Say what you learned, and what changes and what does not.

say: Fractional means working a fixed share of the week for a client. There is no official rate card, so do not copy a number from social media. Calculate your own floor. These figures are illustrative, not market rates.
Ngozi needs 1,400,000 naira a month, including business costs. Of about 20 working days, she expects only 14 to be billable. 1,400,000 divided by 14 gives a day rate floor of 100,000 naira.
A discovery sprint takes about 8 days, so 800,000 naira. She adds 15% for coordination, which is 120,000.
Her quote is 920,000 naira, with 40% at signing and 60% on delivery. Because it is built from real days and real costs, she can explain it calmly.
Write a scope of work with deliverables, exclusions and a change process. When a client asks for something new, never say yes in the meeting. Offer written options first.
Ask for a deposit before you start, and confirm payments in your own banking app, not from screenshots. Never share client data from discovery.

panel.heading: Scope and payment safeguards
items: A change process before extra work
Confirm payments in your bank app

say: Before launch, decide what to measure, and add a guardrail, a number that must not get worse. Halima releases pay on delivery to 1,200 pharmacies. In 30 days, 300 use it. That is 25% adoption.

cards.d: 300 of 1,200 active pharmacies used pay on delivery in the first 30 days.
Second orders within 30 days rose from 38% to 46% for new pharmacies.
Failed deliveries rose, mostly large orders. Lower the limit, add a rider safety rule.

say: Pharmacies placing a second order within 30 days rise from 38% to 46%.

say: But failed deliveries rise from 3% to 5%, mostly large orders where riders carry big sums. So she keeps the feature, lowers the order limit, adds a rider safety rule, and reports honestly that other changes that month may explain part of the gain.

say: Hiring managers want to see how you think. Write two to four pages: the context, your discovery, and how you chose between options.

panel.heading: A case study that shows your thinking

say: Add two or three stories with criteria, then results and reflection. If a decision did not work, say so and show what you learned.

panel.heading: A case study that shows your thinking

say: To remember. Put problems on your roadmap, not features. Explain priority changes early. Price from your own costs and billable days. Handle every scope change in writing. And measure with a guardrail, then report honestly.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Price from your costs and billable days
Written options for every scope change
Measure with a guardrail; report honestly

say: Now practise. Draft a Now-Next-Later roadmap for an organisation you know. Price and scope a discovery sprint. Write a measurement plan with a guardrail, and a 90-day plan in three 30-day blocks.
Share it with someone who will check on you at day 30, and continue with the lessons below.
